item.title: NFL line judge takes knee and appears to pray after umpire collapses during Jaguars-Texans London game
item.description: Umpire Larry Smith collapsed on the Wembley Stadium turf during the Jaguars-Texans game, and the moment that followed moved NFL fans everywhere.
item.content:encoded:
The news surrounding NFL officials has lately not been kind in that there has been fiery criticism and even a couple of suspensions, but on Sunday we saw these people also deserve respect and compassion.

And they give it, too.

During the first quarter of the Jacksonville Jaguars versus Houston Texans game in London, umpire Larry Smith was going about his duties, changing the ball out after a play, when he slipped on the slick Wembley Stadium turf and fell.

Smith got back up under his own power and then collapsed.

It seemed one of his knees buckled.

And as trainers came out to attend to Smith, we saw a reminder that these people so often challenged by coaches and players, and criticized and condemned by fans on social media and other forums, are indeed human.

While Smith lay on the turf getting attention, line judge Carl Johnson came over, took a knee, removed his cap, and began to pray for his fallen friend and colleague.

THE NFL IS AMERICA'S MOST GOD-CENTERED PROFESSIONAL SPORTS LEAGUE AND SUNDAY'S GAMES CONTINUED TO PROVE IT

You see this done by players for one another all the time.

We saw it this year when Jaxson Dart went down for the Giants and again when Jayden Daniels was injured when the Commanders played the Cowboys. Packers players also kneeled to pray for fallen teammate Jayden Reed when he injured his neck earlier this season.

It was moving to see it done by one official for another.

Smith required a cart to leave the field. The report from the NFL Network said Smith suffered a lower-leg injury.

The officiating crew shifted its formation to work the game with six people instead of the regulation seven.

And we have a noteworthy moment that adds context to the other news officials have made this season, including a couple of suspensions on October 5 following Jeff Seeman's cursing at Arizona tight end Trey McBride and Adrian Hill's confrontational behavior in a Minnesota Vikings game.

item.title: LeBron James' wife declines to upgrade best friend's flight, kicking off hot debate
item.description: LeBron James' wife Savannah James and friend April McDaniel wound up kicking off an online debate after discussing how they handle first-class vs. coach seating on trips.
item.content:encoded:
An airplane seating arrangement between two friends has travelers debating whether having a bigger budget means picking up the tab for someone else's upgrade — or not.

Savannah James, entrepreneur and wife of NBA superstar LeBron James, recently discussed how she and her friend April McDaniel handle the difference in their travel budgets when they travel.

Speaking on the "Mental Wealth" podcast, McDaniel said she does not expect to sit in first class simply because Savannah James does.

OUTRAGED PASSENGERS SAY PARENTS DITCHED ROWDY KIDS IN COACH WHILE THEY UPGRADED TO FIRST CLASS

"If we're going on the same trip, I don't feel the need to be in first [class] because that's not in my budget," McDaniel said.

Savannah James said her friends understand that traveling with her does not mean she will automatically cover their expenses.

"My friends are very respectful of my situation," Savannah James said. "There's no expectation of, like, taking care of something or, you know, just having me be responsible for them. It has never, ever been that."

This approach to traveling together has created debate online — with some people questioning whether the wealthier friend should pay the difference so that the group can sit together.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Diane Gottsman, a national etiquette expert and founder of the Protocol School of Texas, told Fox News Digital there's nothing inherently wrong with friends choosing different cabins as long as everyone is comfortable with the arrangement.

"If you have a group of friends, and they are flying coach while you want to fly first class, there's really nothing wrong with it as long as everyone is understanding and agreeable," Gottsman said.

The situation changes, however, if someone feels excluded or uncomfortable, she said.

Even when one traveler has considerably more money to spend, Gottsman said that doesn't make that person responsible for paying to upgrade everyone else.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"It's not an obligation of the person who makes more money to upgrade everyone else," she said. "Just take your seat up front and say you'll see everyone when you land."

The arrangement shared by Savannah James and her friend April McDaniel drew sharply different reactions from travelers online.

One commenter said that while friends should not feel entitled to someone else's money, having significant wealth would make them want to share more of those experiences with people close to them.

"No one is entitled to anything," the Reddit user wrote. 

The person added, "If we're childhood besties, and I have an abundance of wealth, I'm treating my friend to nice experiences!"

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Others saw nothing wrong with friends paying for the level of travel they can each comfortably afford.

"I feel empowered to get what I can afford and not have my friends pay for me just because they have the money," another person wrote. "I'm not her kid."

"It's really not that big of a deal," another user wrote. "It's a plane ride."

Fox News Digital reached out to Savannah James for comment but did not immediately hear back.
